hero.headline: Smith warns Justice Department integrity threatened under Trump
hero.teaser: Former special counsel Jack Smith said the US faces an attack on the rule of law and expressed concern about future elections.
hero.body:
Former special counsel Jack Smith warned that the United States is facing an attack on the rule of law under President Trump, saying he is concerned about the integrity of future elections. Smith accused the administration of weaponizing the Justice Department and argued that judges' distrust of prosecutors is preventing the department from functioning properly.

Smith brought charges against Trump following his first term as special counsel. His comments reflect ongoing tensions between the former prosecutor and the current administration over the role of the Justice Department in investigating political figures and handling cases involving the executive branch.

cards.headline: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill at least 30 in largest attack on capital
cards.body:
Russia launched a large-scale assault on Ukraine's capital overnight, deploying the largest number of weapons used in a single attack on the city. The barrage killed at least 30 people and wounded numerous others across multiple neighborhoods.

The overnight strikes involved ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones targeting the capital. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on social media that the Russian tactics remained consistent: "Strike drones, cruise missiles and a significant amount of ballistics."

He noted that most targets were civilian infrastructure in cities. "Residential buildings, energy, and enterprises have been damaged," Zelenskyy wrote, describing the destruction across Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.

Ukrainian air defense systems worked to intercept incoming weapons throughout the night. The sheer volume of projectiles in this assault appeared to challenge defensive capabilities in some areas. Loud explosions shook Kyiv for hours, with many residents sheltering in subway stations as emergency crews dug through rubble searching for victims.

The attack extended beyond the capital. Russian drones also struck Odesa and Kharkiv, injuring at least three people. Authorities reported repelling more than 600 drones across the country, described as the largest attack in several days.

The death toll makes this one of the deadliest single attacks on Kyiv since Russia's invasion began. Ukrainian officials characterized the assault as unprecedented in scale for strikes specifically targeting the capital. While the city has faced periodic missile and drone attacks throughout the conflict, none had deployed such a large number of weapons across such a wide area.

The overnight assault came after a prisoner exchange on Friday, in which Russia and Ukraine traded 193 service members. These periodic exchanges represented one of the conditions of US-brokered negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv, though the talks have made no progress on key issues regarding ending the invasion.

Russia has maintained its strategy of long-range strikes on Ukrainian population centers despite international criticism of attacks on civilian areas. Ukraine has continued to seek additional air defense systems from Western allies to protect its cities and critical infrastructure against sustained Russian bombardment.

Meanwhile, Ukraine carried out some of its longest-distance drone strikes deep inside Russian territory. In Russia's Belgorod region near the border, a woman was killed and a man seriously injured in a drone strike, demonstrating the expanding scope of the conflict beyond Ukraine's borders.

The continued Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure and population centers represent an escalation in the aerial campaign targeting Ukraine's capital and other major cities as the war continues.

cards.headline: Trump calls current US support for NATO ridiculous ahead of alliance summit
cards.teaser: The former president said maintaining present levels of American support for the military alliance would be ridiculous.
cards.body:
Donald Trump has criticized the United States' relationship with NATO as "one sided" and "ridiculous," saying the military alliance is not reciprocal. Speaking on Truth Social ahead of a NATO summit in Ankara, Trump claimed that NATO members "were not there for us" during the Iran conflict.

Trump has a history of pressuring NATO allies to increase their defense spending contributions. His latest comments come as the alliance prepares for its upcoming summit and faces ongoing discussions about defense spending commitments among European members.

cards.headline: Iran begins public mourning as Ayatollah Khamenei's body lies in state
cards.teaser: The body of Ali Khamenei, killed in February, will lie in state at Tehran's Grand Mosalla ahead of days of funeral events.
cards.body:
Iran has begun public mourning for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, with his body lying in state at Tehran's Grand Mosalla starting Friday. The funeral events are expected to span multiple days as the country honors its deceased Supreme Leader.

The ceremonies are anticipated to draw large crowds. A powerful general appeared in public as Iran prepared for the funeral proceedings. Iranian officials issued warnings to the United States and Israel ahead of the funeral processions, signaling a defiant stance during the mourning period.

cards.headline: States roll back worker heat protections as heat dome spreads across eastern US
cards.body:
A heat dome covering much of the eastern United States has intensified concerns about protecting workers from extreme temperatures at a time when several states have reduced or eliminated heat-related workplace protections.

Florida is among the states that have rolled back heat protections for workers. While many states maintain laws designed to protect employees from heat-related illness and injury, recent legislative changes in some jurisdictions have weakened these safeguards. The timing raises particular concerns as weather patterns expose large populations to sustained high temperatures.

Heat domes occur when high-pressure atmospheric systems trap warm air over a region, creating prolonged periods of elevated temperatures. The current system affecting the eastern US presents significant risks for outdoor workers in construction, agriculture, and other industries where employees face extended exposure to the elements. Worker advocates have pointed to heat protection laws as important safeguards for preventing heat exhaustion, heat stroke, and other potentially fatal conditions.

States that maintain robust heat protection standards typically require employers to provide water, rest breaks, and shade during periods of extreme heat. Some mandate specific temperature thresholds that trigger additional safety protocols. The contrast between states maintaining these protections and those scaling back regulations highlights diverging approaches to workplace safety policy.

Public health experts note that heat-related workplace injuries and deaths tend to increase during prolonged heat events, making protective measures particularly relevant during weather patterns like the current heat dome. The rollbacks have intensified scrutiny of the policy changes, as temperatures remain elevated across the affected region.

The policy debate reflects broader tensions over worker protections. Recent analyses show that enforcement of workplace safety standards has declined significantly in some jurisdictions. The National Labor Relations Board has seen increased dismissals of unfair labor practice charges under new leadership, with dismissal rates rising substantially compared to previous years. Staffing shortages and procedural changes have contributed to fewer charges advancing through the system.

Worker advocates express concern about the cumulative effect of rolled-back protections and reduced enforcement. They argue that weakened standards leave employees vulnerable during weather events that pose genuine health risks. The combination of eliminated heat protections and declining enforcement creates gaps in worker safety across multiple areas.

As the heat dome continues affecting the eastern United States, workers in exposed industries face particular vulnerability. The debate over heat protections reflects larger questions about the role of regulation in workplace safety and the balance between business flexibility and employee welfare. The current weather event has focused renewed attention on these policy choices, with worker safety advocates calling for stronger protections rather than rollbacks during periods of extreme heat.

cards.headline: Dow hits record close as jobs data softens, Nasdaq falls on chip stock decline
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record high Thursday, jumping nearly 600 points, while the Nasdaq declined as semiconductor stocks extended their r.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record high Thursday, gaining nearly 600 points, while the Nasdaq declined as semiconductor stocks fell. The divergence reflected a market rotation away from technology stocks. Employment data showed signs of cooling in the US labor market, which provided some relief to investors concerned about Federal Reserve interest rate policy.

The softer jobs figures suggest the labor market may be moderating, potentially giving the Fed more flexibility in monetary policy. Market analysts noted the data provides both the central bank and investors more time to assess economic conditions. The dollar weakened following the employment report.

cards.headline: Instagram runs ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India
cards.teaser: The platform displayed advertisements using terms like rape and child video that directed users to illegal content on Telegram.
cards.body:
Instagram ran advertisements in India promoting child sexual abuse material, according to BBC findings. The ads contained explicit search terms including "rape" and "child video," and directed users to content hosted on the messaging app Telegram.

The discovery reveals vulnerabilities in Instagram's advertising system, which failed to prevent the placement of ads facilitating access to child exploitation material. The ads leveraged external messaging services to distribute illegal content, highlighting persistent challenges for major social media platforms in preventing the promotion of abuse material.

cards.headline: Syria says bomb blast at Damascus cafe kills nine
cards.teaser: A bombing at a cafe near a major government building in Damascus killed nine people, Syrian state media reported.
cards.body:
Nine people were killed in a bomb blast at a cafe in Damascus near the Palace of Justice, a major government building in the Syrian capital, according to Syrian state media.

No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

cards.headline: China defends ethnic unity law criticized by rights groups and Western officials
cards.teaser: Beijing responded to criticism of a new law that rights groups say threatens Tibetans, Uyghurs and other minorities.
cards.body:
China's new ethnic unity law came into effect despite warnings from Taiwan, the United Nations, and rights groups. The Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress aims to forge a shared national identity among ethnic groups, including by strengthening Mandarin as the official language.

Critics, including overseas human rights campaigners, argue the law will erode the rights of ethnic minorities like Uyghurs and Tibetans. China maintains the measure protects minority groups rather than restricting them.

cards.headline: Venezuela rescues earthquake survivor after eight days trapped under collapsed parking structure
cards.teaser: Rescue teams pulled a man alive from beneath a multi-story car park more than a week after an earthquake struck Venezuela.
cards.body:
Hernán Alberto Gil Flores, a 43-year-old security guard, was rescued alive from the collapsed basement of Galerías Playa Grande shopping centre in La Guaira, Venezuela, eight days after back-to-back earthquakes struck the country. He survived in a pocket of air within his workstation cabin.

The rescue drew cheers from international rescue teams who pulled him from the rubble. When first contacted by rescuers, Gil asked them not to inform his wife, fearing he might not survive the ordeal.

cards.headline: Trump calls current US support for NATO ridiculous ahead of alliance summit
cards.teaser: The former president said maintaining present levels of American support for the military alliance would be ridiculous.

cards.teaser: The body of Ali Khamenei, killed in February, will lie in state at Tehran's Grand Mosalla ahead of days of funeral events.
cards.body:

The ceremonies are anticipated to draw large crowds. A powerful general appeared in public as Iran prepared for the funeral proceedings. Iranian officials issued warnings to the United States and Israel ahead of the funeral processions, signaling a defiant stance during the mourning period.

cards.headline: Instagram ran ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India, investigation finds
cards.teaser: The BBC found advertisements using terms including rape and child video that linked to content on Telegram.
cards.body:
A BBC investigation has found advertisements on Instagram promoting child sexual abuse material in India. The ads contained explicit terms like "rape" and "child video," and directed users to content hosted on the messaging platform Telegram.

The discovery highlights concerns about Instagram's content moderation and advertising approval processes. As a Meta-owned platform, Instagram has faced repeated criticism over its ability to prevent the spread of exploitative material.

cards.headline: Man pleads guilty to faking ransom demand in Nancy Guthrie disappearance case
cards.teaser: Derrick Callella entered a guilty plea for creating a false ransom note in the case of missing woman Nancy Guthrie.
cards.body:
Derrick Callella pleaded guilty to charges related to fabricating a ransom demand in the disappearance case of Nancy Guthrie. The false ransom note was among several communications received during the investigation into Guthrie's disappearance.

The FBI determined that Callella's ransom note was fake. Guthrie's disappearance has stretched over five months, with the sheriff's office and family continuing to seek information about her whereabouts. Some ransom notes in the case remain under investigation as potentially legitimate, according to the FBI.

cards.teaser: Hernn Gil was extracted alive from beneath a collapsed parking structure more than a week after the disaster.
cards.body:
Hernán Alberto Gil Flores, a 43-year-old security guard, was pulled alive from the collapsed basement of Galerías Playa Grande shopping centre in La Guaira eight days after devastating earthquakes struck Venezuela. He had survived in a pocket of air within his workstation cabin.

The rescue drew cheers from international teams at the scene. Finding survivors more than a week after building collapses is exceptionally rare, as survival rates typically drop sharply after the first 72 hours. Gil initially asked rescuers not to inform his wife, fearing he might not survive the extraction.

cards.headline: Former Hong Kong bookseller Lam Wing-kee dies in Taiwan at 70
cards.teaser: Lam was one of five people from Causeway Bay Books who disappeared in 2015 and later described his detention by Chinese authorities.
cards.body:
Lam Wing-kee, a Hong Kong bookseller, has died in Taiwan at the age of 70. He was one of five people associated with Causeway Bay Books who vanished in 2015, an incident that sparked international concern about Beijing's influence over Hong Kong and threats to freedom of expression.

Following his release, Lam shared his account of detention by Chinese authorities, providing a rare firsthand testimony about the circumstances surrounding his disappearance and the treatment he experienced.

cards.headline: Monaco prosecutor issues arrest warrant for suspect in parcel bombing
cards.teaser: The suspect is a foreign national who is no longer in Monaco, according to the prosecutor's office.
cards.body:
Monaco's prosecutor's office has issued an arrest warrant for a suspect in a parcel bombing incident. The suspect is a foreign national who is no longer in Monaco.

The prosecutor's office has not released further details about the bombing or the suspect's whereabouts.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift's wedding celebrations reportedly begin with New York event
cards.teaser: Guests in formal attire, including Lena Dunham and Gigi Hadid, were spotted near Madison Square Garden.
cards.body:
Celebrations for Taylor Swift's rumored wedding kicked off with a star-studded gathering in New York. Actress Lena Dunham, model Gigi Hadid, and music collaborator Jack Antonoff were spotted in formal attire near Madison Square Garden.

Swift and NFL star Travis Kelce have kept details about their upcoming nuptials private, though speculation suggests a multi-day celebration may take place at Madison Square Garden.

hero.headline: Asian markets rebound after semiconductor stocks recover from selloff
hero.teaser: Asian stock markets rallied after an earlier decline, led by South Korean exchanges recovering despite weakness in chip stocks.
hero.body:
Asian markets rallied after oil prices dropped sharply, driven by comments from US President Donald Trump suggesting the conflict with Iran could end soon. The recovery marks a reversal from early losses across the region.

Brent crude fell dramatically from Monday's peak of $119.50 a barrel to approximately $91.70 following Trump's remarks that the war on Iran was "very complete, pretty much." The oil decline eased investor concerns about prolonged energy supply disruptions. South Korea's Kospi index jumped 6%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 2.5% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng closed up 2%.

The Middle East tensions had initially spiked oil prices as concerns grew about potential disruptions to global energy supplies. Approximately one-fifth of global oil and seaborne gas tankers pass through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed for a week. However, Trump's comments offered reassurance to markets worried about extended conflict and sustained energy price increases.

Matt Britzman, senior equity analyst at Hargreaves Lansdown, noted that "what initially looked like a one-way surge in energy costs and the inflation headaches that come with it has started to stabilise, offering some much-needed breathing room."

European markets also responded positively to the de-escalation signals. The FTSE 100 opened about 1.4% higher, while the Stoxx Europe 600 index rose 1.5%.

Despite the market recovery, uncertainty remains about the conflict's trajectory. Trump stated "we have won in many ways" but added "not enough," signaling the situation remains fluid. He also warned Iran via social media that any actions blocking the Strait of Hormuz would result in retaliation "twenty times harder."

Iranian officials have responded with their own threats, with Tehran declaring it would not allow oil exports if US and Israeli attacks continued, according to state media reports.

To manage energy supply concerns, Trump indicated the administration would waive some oil-related sanctions temporarily. The move, made after Trump spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin, could complicate US efforts to maintain sanctions on Moscow over Ukraine. The Trump administration previously permitted Indian refiners to temporarily purchase Russian oil for 30 days.

French President Emmanuel Macron suggested several countries could deploy ships to escort tankers through the region once the conflict's most intense phase concludes.

Despite the price decline from Monday's peaks, oil continues trading approximately 25% higher than levels before the conflict began. Several governments have taken action to address energy concerns, with Croatia, Hungary, South Korea, and Thailand implementing fuel price caps. The Philippines ordered public officials to reduce air conditioning and travel, while Bangladesh closed universities early and advanced holiday periods to conserve electricity and fuel.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record high Thursday, gaining nearly 600 points, while the Nasdaq declined as semiconductor stocks fell. The divergence reflected a market rotation away from technology stocks. Employment data showed signs of cooling in the US labor market, which provided some relief to investors concerned about Federal Reserve interest rate policy.

The softer jobs figures suggest the labor market may be moderating, potentially giving the Fed more flexibility in monetary policy. Market analysts noted the data provides both the central bank and investors more time to assess economic conditions. The dollar weakened following the employment report.

cards.headline: Anthropic relaunches Fable AI model after US lifts export controls
cards.teaser: The Trump administration removed export restrictions on Anthropic's latest Fable and Mythos AI models, allowing the company to relaunch its product.
cards.body:
Anthropic has restored access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models after the US government lifted export controls that had been in place for more than two weeks. The restrictions were imposed due to security concerns that the models could be misused to enable cyber-attacks. US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said the government had worked closely with Anthropic to analyze and approve Fable 5, ensuring alignment across US agencies while strengthening American AI leadership.

The San Francisco company can now distribute its latest models more widely to customers following the government's approval.

cards.headline: Millions of Trump investment accounts signed up ahead of July 4 opening
cards.teaser: More than six million Trump investment accounts have been registered, but some face barriers to accessing the program that opens for contributions on Independence Day.
cards.body:
More than six million children have been signed up for Trump investment accounts, which will begin accepting contributions on July 4. The accounts offer up to $1,000 in benefits for eligible participants.

Some children remain missing out on the accounts due to barriers in the signup process. The program has seen significant uptake since registration opened, though the exact eligibility requirements and distribution methods have created obstacles for certain families seeking to enroll.

cards.headline: Burnham signals limited flexibility on tax policy ahead of likely PM role
cards.teaser: The likely next British prime minister said there is some room for movement on tax policy while pledging to honor Labour's major tax commitments.
cards.body:
Andy Burnham has committed to maintaining Labour's pledges not to raise VAT, income tax, or national insurance contributions as he prepares to become prime minister. These three taxes were central to Labour's election campaign promises.

However, Burnham has suggested there may be some scope for adjustments to other areas of tax policy, indicating he is seeking to balance Labour's campaign commitments with the need for fiscal flexibility in government.

cards.headline: Leading AI researcher launches startup for more flexible artificial intelligence
cards.teaser: Yan LeCun, who says current AI is not truly smart, has founded a startup developing a new approach to artificial intelligence systems.
cards.body:
Yan LeCun, a prominent AI researcher, has started a company working on a more flexible artificial intelligence system. LeCun has been vocal in his assessment that current AI technology is not actually smart.

The startup aims to develop AI systems that go beyond the capabilities of existing models. LeCun's critique of current AI limitations reflects growing discussion in the industry about the next phase of artificial intelligence development and what technical advances will be needed to create more adaptable systems.

cards.headline: California farmer gives away nectarines amid legal dispute over sales rights
cards.teaser: A Reedley farmer is distributing 125,000 pounds of white nectarines for free after a produce company disputed his right to sell the fruit.
cards.body:
A California farmer held a free nectarine giveaway that drew large crowds in Fresno County after receiving a cease and desist order from a food marketing company. The dispute centers on who has exclusive rights to sell white nectarines.

The farmer in Reedley is giving away 125,000 pounds of fruit rather than letting it go to waste during the legal conflict. The cease and desist order from the produce company claims it holds exclusive marketing rights, preventing the farmer from selling his nectarine crop through normal commercial channels.

hero.headline: Scientists build synthetic cell capable of feeding, growing, and reproducing
hero.body:
Researchers have created synthetic cells that can perform fundamental life functions, marking what experts describe as a major breakthrough in artificial biology. The tiny structures, called SpudCells, use lab-made DNA to feed, grow, and multiply in controlled laboratory conditions.

The synthetic cells were constructed from chemical compounds and represent the first known example of artificially created cells that complete a full life cycle, including growth, genetic copying, and division to produce new generations. The work was led by Dr Kate Adamala at the University of Minnesota.

SpudCells begin as miniature water-filled spheres called liposomes, each just a few thousandths of a millimeter wide. Researchers added synthetic DNA to provide basic functions. The cells survive in a nutrient-rich liquid containing essential chemicals like ATP, which supplies energy. To grow, SpudCells fuse with smaller "feeder" liposomes that contain molecules, enzymes, and ribosomes needed for protein production. The synthetic DNA carries instructions for copying the genome and dividing into daughter cells.

The researchers demonstrated that SpudCells with genetic advantages can outcompete others, mimicking natural selection. However, the synthetic cells remain far simpler than natural organisms. They cannot manufacture their own protein-making machinery, regulate their own metabolism, or manage waste. They depend entirely on the surrounding liquid for survival and typically fail after a few generations because they often pass incorrect amounts of DNA to offspring.

Adamala emphasized the significance of the achievement while acknowledging limitations. "It is not as robust, as fast, or as good at most of its functions as a natural cell," she said, "but it is proof of principle that molecules can reconstitute behaviours that up until now we only associated with natural living cells."

The breakthrough could enable the creation of artificial organisms designed to produce drugs, food, fuel, and other materials. Beyond practical applications, the work addresses fundamental questions about what constitutes life and how living systems might have emerged from non-living chemistry.

Professor Tom Ellis from Imperial College London called the work "probably the field's biggest breakthrough in recent times," noting it helps establish the minimum requirements for life and provides a fully understood system for testing biological models.

Adamala and collaborators, including Stanford bioengineer Professor Drew Endy, are establishing an institution called Biotic to advance synthetic cell research. Their goal is to develop what Endy describes as "an operating system for life" built from genes and biochemistry.

Some scientists have raised questions about the approach. Philosopher John Dupré from the University of Exeter suggested synthetic cells may have limited value compared to modified bacteria and questioned whether they truly illuminate the nature of life, particularly regarding the symbiotic relationships characteristic of natural organisms.

cards.headline: European politician investigating spyware had phone hacked with Pegasus
cards.teaser: A government customer of NSO Group used Pegasus spyware to hack the phone of a European politician serving on an EU committee investigating the spyware industry.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

An NSO Group government customer deployed Pegasus spyware against Stelios Kouloglou, a Greek member of the European Parliament, while he was serving on an EU committee investigating spyware abuses. Researchers at the University of Toronto's Citizen Lab documented the repeated attacks on his device.

The investigation could not identify which government operated the spyware, but researchers found the hacking campaign bore similarities to previous Pegasus attacks against exiled Russian and Belarusian journalists in Europe. The incident underscores how commercial spyware has been used to target individuals conducting oversight of the surveillance technology sector.

cards.headline: Apple seeks dismissal of lawsuit over YouTube video training for AI
cards.teaser: Apple has responded to a lawsuit filed by three YouTube channels, asking for the case to be dismissed under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act.
cards.body:
Apple filed a response to a lawsuit brought by three YouTube channels, seeking to have the case dismissed. The lawsuit centers on allegations related to using YouTube videos for artificial intelligence training purposes. Apple argues the case should be dismissed under provisions of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act.

The legal filing represents Apple's formal position in the dispute over how companies can use online video content for machine learning and AI development. The case joins broader debates about copyright protections and the use of publicly available content for training artificial intelligence systems.

cards.headline: Sony to end physical disc production for new PlayStation games in 2028
cards.teaser: Sony announced that physical disc production will end in January 2028 for new games releasing on PlayStation consoles, with the company already repurposing its disc factory.
cards.body:
Sony will stop releasing new PlayStation games on physical discs starting in January 2028. After that date, all new games will be available only through PlayStation Store and digital retailers.

The shift reflects changing consumer preferences toward digital gaming. Retail shops will continue selling PlayStation games, but only in the form of digital codes rather than physical discs. Sony has already begun converting its disc manufacturing facility to other purposes, cementing the company's move away from physical media.

cards.headline: Last-minute technical issue delays NASA satellite rescue mission launch
cards.teaser: A last-minute technical problem halted the launch of a satellite rescue mission intended to service a NASA spacecraft in orbit.
cards.body:
A launch scheduled to send a satellite rescue mission into orbit was delayed due to a technical problem that emerged shortly before liftoff. The mission was designed to service or repair a NASA satellite currently in space.

The delay represents a setback for the planned orbital servicing operation. Launch teams identified the issue during final preparations, forcing a postponement to address the technical concern before attempting another launch.

cards.headline: Zuckerberg tells Meta staff AI agent development slower than expected
cards.teaser: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg told employees at an internal meeting that the company's AI agent development has not progressed as quickly as he had hoped.
cards.body:
Mark Zuckerberg told Meta employees during an internal meeting that the company's AI development efforts are progressing more slowly than he anticipated. The Meta CEO specifically addressed delays in advancing AI agents, a key focus area for the company's technology initiatives.

The admission reflects the significant technical challenges involved in developing autonomous AI systems. As major technology companies race to deploy advanced AI capabilities, Meta's slower-than-expected progress highlights the gap between initial projections and real-world development timelines.

cards.headline: IQM admits uncertain future for quantum computing at public debut
cards.teaser: IQM, a Finnish quantum computing company, went public on Nasdaq at a valuation of about $1.9 billion while acknowledging uncertainty about the technology's future.
cards.body:
IQM, a Finnish quantum computing company, went public on Nasdaq today with a valuation of approximately $1.9 billion, becoming Europe's first publicly traded quantum firm.

The company's public debut marks a significant milestone for the quantum computing sector in Europe.

hero.headline: Chris Froome retires after four Tour de France victories
hero.body:
Chris Froome, Britain's four-time Tour de France champion, has confirmed his retirement from professional cycling at age 41. The announcement came on Friday in Barcelona at the start of this year's Tour, ending what has been described as the longest retirement saga in cycling.

"Unfortunately, there was that fall last summer. That wasn't the way I wanted it to end. But even then, I knew it was over," Froome said when asked about his decision.

Froome's career achievements extended beyond his four Tour victories. He won the 2018 Giro d'Italia and claimed the Vuelta a España titles in 2011 and 2017. For a period in 2018, he held all three Grand Tour titles simultaneously, a rare accomplishment in professional cycling.

The British rider's dominance came primarily during his 11 seasons with Team Sky, from 2010 to 2020, when he served as team leader and established himself as one of the era's most formidable stage racers. His climbing ability and time trial prowess made him particularly dangerous in multi-week races, where he built substantial advantages in the mountains.

However, Froome's final years were marked by decline and injury. His last Grand Tour appearance, the 2022 Vuelta a España, saw him finish 113th overall. In his final professional race at the Tour of Poland two weeks before his crash, he completed 68th overall. Last August, a training accident proved decisive when Froome crashed and was airlifted to hospital with five broken ribs, a spine fracture, a collapsed lung, and a pericardial rupture, a potentially life-threatening tear to the sac surrounding the heart.

The injuries capped a difficult period that began in 2019 when Froome crashed during a time-trial reconnaissance at the Criterium du Dauphiné and was hospitalised. This incident marked the beginning of the end for his and Team Sky's dominance, as younger riders like Tadej Pogacar emerged.

Despite the decline, Froome signed a lucrative contract with Israel-Premier Tech in 2021 but never recovered his winning form. His struggle continued as a team ambassador, with billionaire owner Sylvan Adams publicly questioning his value after Froome was excluded from the 2023 Tour team.

Froome's career was also marked by controversy. In 2018, he received an adverse analytical finding for salbutamol use but was ultimately exonerated after contesting the case with Team Sky's support. The incident fuelled scepticism, particularly in France.

Now remaining in Barcelona as a brand ambassador for Tour sponsors Skoda, Froome watched the 2026 race begin while acknowledging that younger riders like Pogacar now dominate the sport he once controlled.

cards.headline: Switzerland beats Algeria 2-0 to advance at World Cup
cards.teaser: Switzerland ended an 88-year wait for a knockout stage victory at the World Cup with a 2-0 win over Algeria in Vancouver.
cards.body:
Switzerland advanced to the World Cup last 16 with a commanding 2-0 victory over Algeria in Vancouver. Goals from Breel Embolo and Dan Ndoye secured the win, ending Switzerland's 88-year drought without a knockout stage victory at the tournament.

The Swiss produced an impressive performance, with 20-year-old attacker Johan Manzambi playing a key role in the dazzling display. Manzambi has been one of the tournament's standout young talents, scoring three goals in the group stage—only Kylian Mbappé and Thomas Müller have scored more at a World Cup before age 21 this century.

cards.headline: Portugal advances to World Cup last 16 with win over Croatia
cards.teaser: Portugal beat Croatia 2-1 in Toronto to set up a last 16 matchup against Spain after a dramatic second half.
cards.body:
Portugal defeated Croatia 2-1 in a dramatic match in Toronto to secure their place in the knockout rounds. Cristiano Ronaldo and Goncalo Ramos scored for Portugal, while a chaotic second half saw the intensity rise considerably.

The victory sets up a last-16 clash between Iberian rivals Portugal and Spain. Croatia's hopes for a late comeback were dashed when VAR ruled their equalizer offside, ending their World Cup campaign.

cards.headline: Arsenal signs England midfielder Georgia Stanway from Bayern
cards.teaser: England midfielder Georgia Stanway has joined Arsenal from Bayern Munich, saying she wants to win trophies and develop as a player.
cards.body:
Arsenal have signed England midfielder Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich on a permanent deal. The Lioness expressed her pride at joining the club, describing it as "massive" and highlighting its role in driving women's football forward.

Stanway, returning to the Women's Super League after her spell in Germany, is eager to win trophies and develop as a player. She cited Arsenal's backing and fanbase as key factors in her decision to make the move.

cards.headline: Jaylen Brown addresses trade from Celtics to 76ers
cards.teaser: Jaylen Brown said the Celtics showed him a lack of respect before his trade to the Philadelphia 76ers.
cards.body:
The Boston Celtics traded 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers, acquiring Paul George and multiple draft picks in return. Boston received two first-round picks and two second-round picks as part of the deal. Brown had expressed unhappiness with his treatment by the Celtics in the weeks leading up to the trade.

Brown spoke publicly about the move, saying the Celtics demonstrated a lack of respect toward him. He described feeling both excited and disappointed about joining the 76ers, marking the end of his tenure in Boston and the beginning of a new chapter with the division rival.

cards.headline: Alex Ovechkin signs one-year deal to return to Capitals
cards.teaser: Alex Ovechkin, the NHL's all-time goals leader, will return to the Washington Capitals for a 22nd season on a one-year contract.
cards.body:
Alex Ovechkin has agreed to a one-year contract with the Washington Capitals, securing his return for a 22nd NHL season at age 40. The signing keeps the league's all-time goals leader with the franchise where he has spent his entire professional career.

The Capitals structured the deal to fit within their salary cap constraints while retaining their cornerstone player for another season.

cards.headline: Julio Rodriguez enters concussion protocol after helmet hit
cards.teaser: Seattle Mariners outfielder Julio Rodriguez entered concussion protocol after a throw struck the back of his helmet during a game against the Angels.
cards.body:
Julio Rodriguez left the Seattle Mariners' game against the Los Angeles Angels after being hit in the back of the helmet by a throw. The outfielder subsequently entered concussion protocol as a precautionary measure.

Victor Robles also exited the same game with an arm injury, though X-rays on his arm came back negative. The Mariners lost two players to injuries in the same contest, with Rodriguez's status now dependent on concussion protocol evaluations.

hero.headline: Madonna Releases Confessions II Album to Critical Acclaim
hero.body:
Madonna has released Confessions II, her 15th studio album, which critics are hailing as her strongest work in two decades. The album serves as a follow-up to her 2005 release Confessions on a Dance Floor, arriving 21 years later.

According to Madonna, the project was inspired by her 2023 Celebration tour, which led her to reflect on her career history. The album draws heavily from that past, referencing not only Confessions on a Dance Floor but also other periods of her artistic evolution, including the trip-hop influences of Bedtime Stories and the spiritual elements of Ray of Light.

The album opens with "I Feel So Free," where Madonna considers creating new personas and identities. Musically, Confessions II features old-school dance influences rather than contemporary trends. The production incorporates Chicago house music, UK garage, and 1990s trip-hop aesthetics, drawing from classic records by artists like Lil Louis and Inner City. The downtempo tracks carry a distinctly 90s mood with breakbeats and atmospheric production.

Producer Stuart Price collaborates with Madonna on material where she appears more comfortable than on previous projects that attempted to incorporate trap or Latin pop. The album's instrumental passages run long in the style of extended remixes, reflecting confidence in the songwriting and production choices.

Lyrically, Madonna explores vulnerability alongside her characteristic confidence. The album includes vivid narratives set in 1980s New York, such as "Danceteria," which references the famous Manhattan nightclub and names figures like Jean-Michel Basquiat and Keith Haring. "LES Girl" recalls a bohemian ex-partner, while "Fragile" serves as an emotional tribute to her late brother Christopher, exploring their complicated relationship.

"The Test," a duet with her daughter Lourdes, carries maternal reflection, with Madonna acknowledging the impact of fame on her child. The collaboration with Sabrina Carpenter on "Bring Your Love" questions motivations behind artistic choices.

The Guardian's review notes that while Confessions II runs nearly 10 minutes longer than the original album and contains some weaker house tracks, it represents Madonna's best work since Confessions on a Dance Floor. Though it lacks a definitive pop hit comparable to "Hung Up," the album demonstrates artistic vitality.

Critics from Variety, Pitchfork, and BBC have published positive assessments, with multiple outlets describing the project as her strongest release in approximately 20 years. The reception positions Confessions II as a significant moment in Madonna's career, potentially appealing to longtime fans while winning back listeners who drifted away during her recent albums.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Wedding Celebration Begins in New York
cards.teaser: Celebrities including Lena Dunham, Gigi Hadid, and Jack Antonoff were spotted in formal attire near Madison Square Garden.
cards.body:
Reports indicate that Taylor Swift's wedding celebration has begun with a star-studded gathering in New York. Actress Lena Dunham, model Gigi Hadid, and longtime music collaborator Jack Antonoff were spotted in formal attire near Madison Square Garden.

Preparations were underway at the venue, with streets around the arena closed to traffic. Catering deliveries included chicken wings and ground beef, along with items from a Brooklyn bakery, suggesting an elaborate event in the midst of a summer heatwave and Independence Day celebrations.

cards.headline: UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy Leaves X Over Abuse and Misinformation
cards.teaser: Lisa Nandy announced her departure from the social media platform and said the Department for Culture, Media and Sport will also leave.
cards.body:
Lisa Nandy, the UK's Culture Secretary, announced she is leaving X, the social media platform owned by Elon Musk. Her department, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport, will also cease using the platform.

Nandy cited concerns that X "now favours abuse and misinformation over meaningful debate" and stated the platform "isn't healthy for our democracy." She highlighted worries about how the site prioritizes far-right and racist content that fuels violence and division. Her department is the UK's second to quit X over these concerns.

cards.headline: British Romantic Drama Secures UK and Ireland Distribution
cards.teaser: My Indian Boyfriend: The Golden Mile will be released theatrically through RFT Films ahead of filming this summer.
cards.body:
My Indian Boyfriend: The Golden Mile, a British romantic drama set during Leicester's Diwali celebrations, has secured theatrical distribution in the UK and Ireland through RFT Films. The deal was announced ahead of the film's principal photography, scheduled to begin this summer.

Directed by Vijay Chauhan, the independent production brings together talent from the UK, Malaysia, Hong Kong, and India. The film will be produced as an international collaboration across these territories.

cards.headline: Vietnam Sales Agent Secures Distribution Deal for Streaming Originals
cards.teaser: Skyline Media will represent more than 20 original miniseries from Galaxy Play in international markets.
cards.body:
Vietnam-based sales agent Skyline Media has partnered with streaming platform Galaxy Play to bring its original content to international audiences. Skyline Media will serve as the exclusive international sales agent for more than 20 Galaxy Play Original miniseries, marking the first time the streaming service's productions will be available outside Vietnam.

The partnership was announced at the Danang Asian Film Festival's DANAFF Industry Days. The slate includes titles such as "Brothers for Life" and "Thousand Dollar Baby," expanding Galaxy Play's global footprint through the collaboration.

cards.headline: AI-Created Indian Musical Releases Opening Track
cards.teaser: Angaat Aalay Ka, the debut song from Mohini Khud Se Pyaar, draws from Maharashtra folk traditions.
cards.body:
Equinox Virtual released Angaat Aalay Ka, the opening song from the AI-created musical microdrama Mohini Khud Se Pyaar. The Indian company was conceived by producer and storyteller Amita Madhvani.

Rooted in Maharashtra's folk traditions, the song arrives at a pivotal moment in the drama's narrative. The track represents the debut musical release from the AI-generated production, which incorporates cultural elements from western India.

cards.headline: Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds in Upstate New York During Swift Wedding
cards.teaser: Multiple outlets reported the couple's location as Taylor Swift's wedding celebration began in New York City.
cards.body:
Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds were seen in upstate New York as Taylor Swift's wedding celebration began in New York City. Multiple media outlets, including TMZ and People, reported on the couple's location during the festivities.

The reports prompted speculation about Lively's friendship with Swift, with some outlets describing the absence as indicating a friendship fallout. Lively and Swift have been photographed together at various events over the years.

hero.headline: Smith warns Justice Department integrity threatened under Trump
hero.teaser: Former special counsel Jack Smith said the US faces an attack on the rule of law and expressed concern about future elections.
hero.body:
Former special counsel Jack Smith warned that the United States is facing an attack on the rule of law under President Trump, saying he is concerned about the integrity of future elections. Smith accused the administration of weaponizing the Justice Department and argued that judges' distrust of prosecutors is preventing the department from functioning properly.

Smith brought charges against Trump following his first term as special counsel. His comments reflect ongoing tensions between the former prosecutor and the current administration over the role of the Justice Department in investigating political figures and handling cases involving the executive branch.

cards.headline: Mitch McConnell remains hospitalized after medical episode
cards.teaser: Former Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell remains hospitalized following a medical episode, his office confirmed Thursday.
cards.body:
Former Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell remains hospitalized following a medical episode, his office confirmed Thursday. The Kentucky Republican, who has served in the Senate since 1985 and led the Republican conference for 16 years before stepping down as leader in January, was admitted to the hospital, though his office did not disclose the nature of the medical episode or details about his condition.

McConnell, 84, has experienced several public health incidents in recent years. In March 2023, he suffered a concussion and fractured rib after falling at a hotel in Washington. Later that year, he twice froze while speaking to reporters, raising questions about his health. Despite these episodes, McConnell continued serving as Republican leader through the end of 2024 before handing the position to his successor.

The senator has been a central figure in Republican politics for decades, shaping conservative judicial appointments and legislative strategy. His tenure as majority leader saw the confirmation of three Supreme Court justices and numerous federal judges. After stepping down from leadership, McConnell retained his seat representing Kentucky and continues to serve on several Senate committees.

McConnell's office has not provided a timeline for his release from the hospital or indicated whether the hospitalization would affect his Senate duties. The lack of details about his condition follows a pattern of limited disclosure during previous health incidents. His staff has historically provided minimal information about his medical situations, offering updates only when necessary.

The hospitalization comes as the Senate prepares for the Independence Day recess. McConnell's colleagues from both parties have not yet issued public statements about his condition. As one of the longest-serving senators in American history, McConnell's health has become a subject of interest given his influential role in shaping legislative outcomes and his status as a senior member of the Republican conference.

cards.headline: Democrats face internal divisions ahead of House midterm push
cards.teaser: Infighting within the Democratic Party could complicate efforts to reclaim the House majority in the fall elections.
cards.body:
Democrats are hoping to win back the House majority this fall, but infighting within the party could complicate their plans. Internal divisions threaten to undermine the unified front Democrats need to present to voters as they work toward November's elections.

Party leaders must navigate these internal tensions while maintaining focus on their broader electoral strategy. The fighting within Democratic ranks could potentially derail their efforts to regain control of the House.

cards.headline: Jeffries discusses Democratic strategy for midterm elections
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries outlined the Democratic Party's approach to the upcoming midterm elections.
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York discussed the Democratic Party's midterm future ahead of America's 250th birthday. Jeffries addressed the party's electoral strategy and priorities as Democrats work to regain control of the House.

The minority leader's comments come as his party navigates the challenges of opposition status while attempting to position itself for gains in the fall elections. Jeffries has led House Democrats since taking over the leadership position, succeeding Nancy Pelosi as the top Democrat in the chamber.

cards.headline: Trump to deliver speech despite extreme heat warning at National Mall
cards.teaser: President Trump said he will proceed with his address at the July 4 celebration despite forecasts of 107-degree temperatures.
cards.body:
Organizers of the Freedom 250 event have delayed entry to the National Mall for a July 4 fireworks show due to extreme heat affecting Washington, D.C. The celebration, marking Independence Day and the nation's 250th anniversary, is planned as a record-breaking fireworks display.

President Trump said he will still deliver a speech at the Salute to America 250 Celebration despite forecasts predicting temperatures will reach 107 degrees during the event. Organizers adjusted entry times in response to the heat advisory.

cards.headline: Rubio comments on US soccer team's World Cup red card
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US men's national soccer team was unfairly penalized during their World Cup match.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized the officiating in the US men's national soccer team's World Cup match, saying the team "got screwed" when striker Folarin Balogun received a red card. Rubio praised the USMNT's overall performance despite the controversial call.

The red card became a point of contention following the match. Rubio joined other observers in questioning the referee's decision during the game.

cards.headline: Colorado Democratic nominee criticizes DSA candidate over antisemitism stance
cards.teaser: Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser said he would confront congressional candidate Melat Kiros for refusing to condemn a firebomb attack as antisemitic.
cards.body:
Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser, who defeated Senator Michael Bennett in the Democratic gubernatorial primary, said he would confront congressional candidate Melat Kiros for refusing to condemn the deadly 2025 firebomb attack on Jewish activists in Boulder as antisemitic. Kiros, a democratic socialist and former attorney, won an upset victory against incumbent Representative Diana DeGette.

Weiser's statement highlights tensions within Colorado's Democratic Party over how candidates address antisemitism. The 2025 Boulder attack targeted Jewish activists, and Kiros's refusal to characterize it as antisemitic has drawn criticism from other Democrats in the state ahead of the general election.
